description: Description Job Title: Software Engineer - Java Employment Type: Permanent Work Location: Chennai India - Hybrid About CloudBees CloudBees helps organizations build, run, and govern software factories, giving enterprises the confidence to ship software better, faster, and safer. Writing code is no longer the bottleneck. Governing what reaches production and validating its impact is. As enterprises adopt agentic coding, software is created faster than most teams can review, secure, and validate. Without consistent governance, organizations risk shipping code they cannot explain, audit, or trust. CloudBees addresses this challenge without asking teams to replace the tools they already use. Across every toolchain a customer runs, CloudBees makes each change, human or AI, visible, auditable, and accountable before it reaches production. CloudBees Unify is the product behind this: a governance layer, with context and control-plane capabilities, that enforces consistent policy and evidence across every tool, team, and workflow. Founded in 2010, CloudBees is backed by Goldman Sachs, Morgan Stanley, Bridgepoint Capital, HSBC, Golub Capital, Delta-v Capital, Matrix Partners, and Lightspeed Venture Partners. Visit us at www.cloudbees.com. About The Role We use Claude Code every day and are pushing agentic AI further into how we work. If you want to be on a team figuring out what AI-assisted engineering actually looks like on a real, complex product (not a sandbox), this is it. CDRO (Continuous Delivery & Release Orchestration) is CloudBees' enterprise CD product. It's been running in production at some of the world's largest engineering orgs for over a decade. Hundreds of engineers depend on it to ship software safely and on schedule. We're a team of about 10, distributed across India, France, Spain, and the US. We're not chasing the next hype cycle feature. We operate a product real customers depend on, modernize it while keeping it stable, and do it with a small team that takes ownership seriously. Key Responsibilities Most teams try AI coding tools on greenfield work. We're doing something harder: applying them to a decade-old enterprise codebase with real customers depending on it. CDRO's core is Java 21 with a significant Groovy layer. The work is a mix of internal cleanup that makes the codebase easier to evolve, and direct improvements that make customers' lives better. Concretely: Own Java work across the core: REST API, pipeline execution engine, persistence layer Continuously reduce complexity: modernize older subsystems, shrink the product surface area where it makes sense, improve test coverage, and leave the codebase easier than you found it Use Claude Code as a normal part of your workflow, to move faster without skipping thought Write tests that prove things work. Shift-left, not "QA will catch it." Document what you build. We're async across timezones. If you know something the team needs to know, write it down. Actively avoid being a single point of failure for anything you own Qualifications Required: Solid Java. You've worked professionally at least 4 years developing Java software, in production codebases that weren't yours, in systems that mattered if they broke. Strong AI awareness: you know what Claude Code, or Cursor, etc. do. You've played with some of them at least. Relational database experience: SQL, JPA/Hibernate, schema migrations. Oracle or PostgreSQL background is a strong advantage. Comfort in large, mature codebases. You can navigate unfamiliar code, form a hypothesis, test it, and stay functional when you don't understand everything at once. Testing discipline. You write unit and integration tests as part of the work, not after. Honest communication. If something is blocked or broken, we need to know. We're async and distributed. Strong plus: Active use of Claude Code to ship real work, not just tab completion. Bonus: you want to push it much further than you do today. Groovy. Willingness to pick it up fast matters more than prior credentials. Kubernetes/Helm: deploying and debugging workloads, not just using them. Experience evolving established systems: migrations, incremental rewrites, dependency upgrades. Preferred (not mandatory): Jenkins or CI/CD internals Distributed systems infrastructure: message brokers (ActiveMQ, Artemis, RabbitMQ), coordination (Zookeeper) React/TypeScript: the UI is adjacent and not your main domain, but not being afraid of it helps Who This Is For You're a Java engineer who finds large, evolved codebases interesting rather than off-putting. You've seen what breaks when systems are poorly documented and owned by one person. You build the opposite. You want hard engineering problems, real ownership, and a team that says what's true. With ~10 people on the team, you'll touch meaningful parts of the system fast. You'd rather evolve a product real enterprises depend on than build a greenfield service nobody's relying on yet. title: Java Developer
description: About the role eG Innovations is a product company looking for a Java Developer who enjoys solving hard, open-ended problems. This role is 100% research-driven: you will investigate unknowns, prototype ideas and turn findings into production-grade product features. No two weeks look the same. You will dig into JVM internals, performance bottlenecks and complex runtime behaviour, and help shape how our product observes and diagnoses Java applications. Location: [Hybrid] • Experience: 57 years • Employment type: Full-time Key responsibilities Research, prototype and evaluate new approaches for the product, then take the winning ideas into production-quality Java code. Perform in-depth troubleshooting of Java applications: memory leaks, thread contention, deadlocks, GC pauses, class-loading issues and CPU hotspots. Analyse heap dumps, thread dumps, GC logs and JFR recordings to find root causes, and document findings clearly. Explore JVM internals, bytecode instrumentation and agent-based techniques where the product needs them. Run proof-of-concepts and benchmarks, and present results with data to product and engineering leads. Design and build features that are performant, observable and reliable at scale. Stay current with the Java ecosystem and observability space, and bring new ideas to the team. Collaborate with product, QA and fellow engineers in a fast-moving, changing environment. Required skills and qualifications Minimum 5 to maximum 7 years of hands-on experience in Core Java (Java 11+; Java 17/21 preferred). Strong grasp of JVM internals: memory model, garbage collectors (G1, ZGC, Shenandoah), JIT compilation and class loading. Proven in-depth Java troubleshooting in production: memory leaks, OutOfMemoryErrors, high CPU, thread deadlocks and latency spikes. Hands-on with diagnostic tools such as jstack, jmap, jcmd, Java Flight Recorder, JDK Mission Control, VisualVM, Eclipse MAT or async-profiler. Solid knowledge of multithreading, concurrency and performance tuning. Experience with Spring / Spring Boot, REST APIs and microservices. Comfortable with Linux, Git, Maven or Gradle, and debugging in containerised environments (Docker, Kubernetes). A research mindset: curious, self-driven, comfortable with ambiguity and able to explain findings clearly. Bachelors or Master’s degree in Computer Science or a related field, or equivalent experience. Added advantage OpenTelemetry (OTEL): hands-on with the OTEL Java agent, SDK, manual and auto-instrumentation, context propagation and the OTEL Collector. Monitoring and observability: experience with metrics, logs and distributed tracing using tools such as Prometheus, Grafana, Jaeger, Zipkin, Elastic/ELK, Datadog, New Relic, Dynatrace or AppDynamics. Familiarity with Java agents, bytecode manipulation (ByteBuddy, ASM, Javassist) or the JVMTI. Understanding of APM concepts: SLIs/SLOs, alerting, and dashboards that lead to faster root-cause analysis. Contributions to open-source projects, technical blogs or conference talks on Java performance or observability. Who will thrive here You will enjoy this role if you would rather chase down why a JVM behaves strangely than repeat the same CRUD feature. You like freedom to experiment, and you take ownership from idea to shipped product. What we offer Fully research-oriented work on a core product, with real influence on its direction. Time and room to explore new technologies and build proof-of-concepts. A collaborative team of engineers who value deep technical work.
